predecessor.failure: The solver elongated frozen dorsal components 2 and 4 by 4.722846545 even though the fixed side views show those sheets are the rear panels of the first dorsal assembly. This created an extra rectangular sail. Frozen component 1 is the caudal sickle-shaped second dorsal and is already close to the declared 0.18 FL target.

solver.method: binary search against the final root-pinned metric after visual identity review of the disconnected dorsal structures
solver.reason: Connected-component pairing alone was insufficient. Candidate A proved that two mirrored sheets can be adjoining panels of the first dorsal rather than a separate second dorsal.
solver.selectionRule: Preserve the two anterior paired groups as one first-dorsal assembly; select the caudal-most dorsal group as the second dorsal even when it is one watertight component rather than two disconnected sheets.

bodyPolicy.caudalFade: zero body-depth correction at and behind the inferred fork
bodyPolicy.headFade: return smoothly to the frozen snout

finPolicy.pectoral: extend each connected side-fin component away from its shared body root; root vertices remain pinned
finPolicy.secondDorsal: extend only frozen component 1, the caudal sickle-shaped structure, from its actual baseline height to 0.18 FL; root vertices remain pinned
finPolicy.anal: extend only the connected anal component with the greatest ventral height; root vertices remain pinned
finPolicy.firstDorsal: retain frozen components 0, 3, 2 and 4 as the complete first-dorsal assembly without independent elongation
finPolicy.finlets: do not change counts or independently rescale
